title: Snakes and Ladders
summary: Given an n x n integer matrix board where cells are labeled from 1 to n^2 in a Boustrophedon style starting from the bottom left (i.e., board[n - 1][0]) and alternating direction each row, you start on square 1.
statement: Given an n x n integer matrix board where cells are labeled from 1 to n^2 in a Boustrophedon style starting from the bottom left (i.e., board[n - 1][0]) and alternating direction each row, you start on square 1. In each move, you roll a die to determine your next square, which must be between curr and curr + 6. If your destination square has a snake or ladder, you must move to the destination of that snake or ladder. The game ends when you reach square n^2. Return the least number of dice rolls required to reach square n^2, or -1 if it is impossible.
constraints: Square numbers follow alternating left-to-right and right-to-left rows from the bottom.
Each move rolls one through six, then follows at most one snake or ladder at the landing square.
Return the minimum moves to reach n squared, or -1.
hints: Convert a square label to its board row and alternating-direction column.
Breadth-first search labels; each state has up to six landings followed by one optional jump.
All rolls cost one, so the first visit to the final label uses the fewest rolls.
editorial: All rolls cost one, so the first visit to the final label uses the fewest rolls.

tests.explanation: Ladders shorten the minimum route to four rolls.
One roll reaches label two, whose ladder reaches three; a second reaches four.
